Which events need a ticket?

Performances are ticketed, and each event has its own price. Workshops, talks, exhibitions and film screenings are free, but you need to register for a place.

You can do both on this page: open any event in the programme.

How do I get my ticket?

Book or register on the event's page. You get an e-ticket for each seat. Venue directions and entry requirements are sent to you in advance.

Where do things happen?

Everything is inside the Arts Council grounds: Auditorium 1, Auditorium 2, Studio 1, Studio 2, the Basement Studio, the Library, the Art Gallery, Jaun Elia Lawn, the Z.A. Bukhari Amphitheatre and Burns Garden. Each event page names its space.

Can I bring children?

Yes. Children's theatre runs on weekday mornings and is mostly booked by schools as groups, with some public tickets. To book for a school, call 021-111-227-544.

Can I take photos?

You can photograph and post, subject to each venue's rules. The festival hashtag is #WCF2026.

Parking, accessibility and refunds

The Arts Council is confirming these details and will add them here before the festival opens. Until then, call 021-111-227-544 or write to info@acpkhi.com.

About the festival

The World Culture Festival brings artists, creators and producers from around the world to Karachi to share their cultures and make art together. Pakistan's own traditions sit at the centre of the programme.

This third edition runs for 25 days across theatre, music, dance, visual arts and film. Its theme is global peace, environment and humanity.

About the Arts Council of Pakistan, Karachi

Top partners: Arts Council of Pakistan, Karachi; Government of Sindh; Geo. Powered by iTecknologi. Confectionery partner: EBM. Food partner: McDonald's.
